summary: The passage describes a labor market undergoing compositional deterioration where employers adjust by reducing hours (shifting from full-time to part-time employment) rather than conducting layoffs. Low real wage growth (1.1%) compresses household purchasing power and drives down the personal savings rate. Meanwhile, nominal wage growth (4.3%) outpaces labor productivity growth (0.9%), widening unit labor costs by 3.2% and sustaining upward pressure on services-sector prices. The observed wage stickiness is attributed—with uncertainty—to potential drivers including labor market tightness, anchored inflation expectations from the pandemic, or structural supply-side rigidities stemming from demographic changes and reduced prime-age labor force participation.
